summary: API gateway backpressure amplification from slow serving-runtime causing cascading 502/504s for a dedicated tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 09:30 UTC IconicHealth saw a sharp spike in 5xx responses (502/504) originating at the API gateway in front of their dedicated capacity. The spike lasted ~45 minutes with intermittent recoveries, and customers reported failed streaming sessions and generator timeouts. Impact: Multiple production requests for IconicHealth returned 502 or 504. End-users saw feature timeouts and degraded throughput; billing was not impacted but customer SLA was at risk. Environment: Dedicated capacity (tenant: iconichealth-prod) in us-east-1, running runtime v1.9.2, API gateway cluster agw-prod-eus-1. Observed behavior: API gateway logs show increased upstream 502s and 504s, often followed by a burst of retries from clients. Serving runtime logs show long tail request latencies for a subset of model shards and occasional worker exit code 137 during the period. Expected behavior: Stable 2xx/streaming responses under the committed throughput; gateway should apply backpressure without cascading failures. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send parallel streaming requests at the customer's typical concurrency mix (50 short chat + 10 long completion). 2) Simulate occasional long-tail 1–2s KV cache miss on shard leader. 3) Observe gateway and runtime behavior; note whether gateway connection pool saturates and retries cascade. Reproducible: Yes under load/test harness that reproduces IconicHealth traffic shape.

comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported export of SDK logs and example request ids at 09:31 UTC. Initial triage shows gateway 5xx correlates with runtime long tail latencies.

SRE (Miguel): Observed connection pool exhaustion on agw-prod-eus-1 for tenant iconichealth. Some keepalive pools dropped to 0 during bursts. Kicking off immediate mitigation: increase per-tenant proxy pool and enable drain-safe mode for warm restarts.

Eng (Priya): Runtime telemetry shows periodic GC/compaction spikes on worker 3 associated with large attention caches. Hypothesis: long-tail requests + small connection pool -> amplification of retries and proxy saturation.
Support (Aisha): Customer is on dedicated, requests urgency. P1 declared; applied temporary concurrency cap on the tenant to protect cluster while mitigation proceeds.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Small per-tenant connection pool combined with long-tail runtime work causes the gateway to queue requests; clients retry aggressively and amplify load. 2) Runtime worker GC/compaction or KV cache miss causes 1–3s stalls that accumulate across shards. 3) Keepalive misconfiguration caused upstream connections to close and recreate frequently, increasing CPU and latency. Findings: - Host-level metrics show p95 runtime CPU jump and increased context-switching at spike time. - No clear OOMs except a single worker exit 137 (investigating whether cgroup eviction happened). - Proxy metrics show pool_exhausted counter correlates with upstream_5xx. Quick experiment: increasing per-tenant proxy pool from 20->80 reduced immediate 502s in testing but did not eliminate long tail latencies. Need runtime patch and client retry smoothing to fully resolve.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 12:10 UTC): 1) Increased API gateway per-tenant proxy connection pool for iconichealth and bumped keepalive timeout. 2) Applied temporary per-tenant concurrency limit at the edge to flatten bursts. 3) Rolled a runtime patch to v1.9.3 on the dedicated cluster that reduces KV cache compaction pauses (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123). 4) Asked IconicHealth to apply client-side retry exponential backoff fixes. Outcome: 502/504 rate dropped to baseline within ~20 minutes after mitigation; post-incident p95 latency improved by ~40% for the tenant. Follow-ups: - Add metrics and alert for proxy_pool_exhausted per-tenant (task INT-920). - Implement adaptive proxy pool auto-scaling and add unit tests for connection reuse (planned PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/789). - Add a runbook step to cap tenant concurrency automatically when pool_exhausted > threshold.
follow_up_tasks: PROJ-344: adaptive proxy pool autoscaling design
SUP-53903: customer follow-up for SDK retry policy guidance
resolution_status: Partial fix deployed; monitoring in prod. Customer notified and accepted workaround pending permanent infra changes.
postmortem_plan: If errors recur, open a Sev1 postmortem. Collect heap profiles for runtime workers and add end-to-end tracing from API gateway to runtime shards. Schedule a cross-team retro with SRE, runtime, and proxy owners within 72 hours.
